method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)' (approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025)), 22 claims; LICENCE: © 2024 American Academy of Ophthalmology, all rights reserved. Site terms: 'This content may not be reproduced, copied, or put into any artificial intelligence program, including large language and generative AI models, without permission from the Academy.' Used in paraphrase mode under the owner decision of 2026-09-23 not to exclude sources for AI-use clauses. (read at PDF front matter (© notice) and the aao.org page footer / https://www.aao.org/terms-of-service). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from The Royal College of Ophthalmologists (UK), RVO Guidelines 2022/SCI/359 'Clinical Guidelines: Retinal Vein Occlusion (RVO)' (January 2022 (date of review January 2025; PDF re-posted June 2026)), 12 claims; LICENCE: © The Royal College of Ophthalmologists 2022. All rights reserved. For permission to reproduce any of the content contained herein please contact contact@rcophth.ac.uk (read at the PDF front matter (https://www.rcophth.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Retinal-vein-occlusion-guideline.pdf)). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the Royal College of Ophthalmologists RVO guideline (2022), paraphrased and hash-anchored, for the systemic work-up, dosing and stopping rules, ischaemic CRVO surveillance, branch-occlusion laser criteria and service standards. S1 claims and anchors are unchanged. The preferred Australian source (Cornish et al., Clin Exp Ophthalmol 2023, CC BY) was retried on 2026-09-24: Wiley still served a bot challenge, Unpaywall lists only the publisher copy, and it is not in PMC, so it was not used.

claims.claim: **Outlook depends on where the vein is blocked and how ischaemic the retina is:** distal, less ischaemic occlusions do better. Central and hemi-central occlusions behave alike, are linked with glaucoma and carry more risk of anterior-segment new vessels and neovascular glaucoma than branch occlusions, so keep eye pressure controlled.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The first examination and imaging should decide:** branch, hemi or central occlusion; whether there is macular oedema; how much ischaemia; and whether new vessels are present on the retina or iris.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine for:** a relative afferent pupillary defect (reflects ischaemia and predicts new vessels); fine new iris vessels on slit lamp; pressure; and gonioscopy before dilating, above all in ischaemic central occlusion, raised pressure or high risk of iris new vessels.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **OCT is the key test for finding and measuring macular oedema, and it drives decisions to re-inject or change treatment**, though retinal thickness does not always match visual acuity.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fluorescein angiography needs informed consent (death occurs in about 1 in 200,000).** Ask women of childbearing age about pregnancy and breastfeeding and use it only when truly needed.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Work with the GP:** RVO raises the risk of an occlusion in the other eye and of cardiovascular disease and stroke. **Under 50, consider haematology or general-medicine referral for a clotting work-up.**
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hypertension accounts for about 48% of RVO, high lipids 20% and diabetes 5%.** Control them, although it is unproven that doing so improves vision or complications.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Eye-clinic tests (RCOphth, S2):** history, blood pressure, blood glucose, full blood count and ESR; further tests and risk-factor care, such as help to stop smoking, sit best with the patient's own doctor. Diabetes is no commoner in RVO, but testing at diagnosis finds undiagnosed cases.
claims.locator: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists (UK), RVO Guidelines 2022/SCI/359, 'Clinical Guidelines: Retinal Vein Occlusion (RVO)', January 2022 (date of review January 2025; PDF re-posted June 2026), https://www.rcophth.ac.uk/guidance-resources/retinal-vein-occlusion-guideline/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **No antiphospholipid testing after an isolated RVO** without other features of antiphospholipid syndrome (S2). A thrombophilia result changes neither treatment nor outlook, and good evidence for anticoagulants or antiplatelet drugs in RVO is lacking.
claims.locator: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists (UK), RVO Guidelines 2022/SCI/359, 'Clinical Guidelines: Retinal Vein Occlusion (RVO)', January 2022 (date of review January 2025; PDF re-posted June 2026), https://www.rcophth.ac.uk/guidance-resources/retinal-vein-occlusion-guideline/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **RVO under 50 is uncommon** (about 0.26% at ages 30–39 and 0.44% at 40–49). Young people with central occlusion need anti-VEGF less often, yet at least 20% end with poor vision from severe neovascular complications.
claims.locator: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists (UK), RVO Guidelines 2022/SCI/359, 'Clinical Guidelines: Retinal Vein Occlusion (RVO)', January 2022 (date of review January 2025; PDF re-posted June 2026), https://www.rcophth.ac.uk/guidance-resources/retinal-vein-occlusion-guideline/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Intravitreal anti-VEGF is first-line for macular oedema in both branch and central occlusion.** Intravitreal steroids work but are second-line because they cause glaucoma and cataract; laser has a limited role in branch occlusion.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Four anti-VEGF agents are in routine use:** ranibizumab, aflibercept 2 mg and faricimab (FDA-approved) and bevacizumab (off-label, with supporting evidence). In trials, 8 mg of aflibercept given 8-weekly was noninferior to 4-weekly 2 mg, after 3–5 monthly loading doses.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not delay treatment.** In BRAVO, eyes first given sham and treated later never caught up with eyes treated from the start.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Faricimab:** in BALATON (branch) and COMINO (central), 6 monthly doses of faricimab 6 mg were noninferior to aflibercept 2 mg for vision at week 24; treatment then moved to treat-and-extend at intervals of up to 16 weeks.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Expect long treatment:** about half of branch and 56% to 75% of central occlusions still need anti-VEGF for oedema more than 5 years after starting.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Before every intravitreal injection, use a topical antiseptic such as povidone-iodine;** routine antibiotic drops are not advised. Serious injection harms are uncommon: endophthalmitis, cataract, retinal detachment, raised pressure.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Systemic safety:** anti-VEGF drugs carry a theoretical risk of arterial clots, but meta-analyses have not shown more major cardiovascular events or deaths.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Branch occlusion: start with anti-VEGF.** Consider steroids and/or grid laser when the response fails or falls short.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Steroid options:** in SCORE (central occlusion), triamcinolone 1 mg was preferred to 4 mg, which caused the most cataract and pressure rise. The dexamethasone implant's benefit rose from day 30, peaked at 90 days and was gone by 6 months; COBALT re-treated as often as every 4 months in branch occlusion.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Overall, pressure rise and cataract with steroids make anti-VEGF the better first treatment.**
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Grid laser can be considered in branch occlusion with a perfused macula, oedema and vision of 20/40 or worse,** but anti-VEGF gives more gain and is preferred unless contraindicated. Laser suits patients who cannot attend monthly (review 3 months later). Adding laser to anti-VEGF gives no extra benefit.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Central occlusion: focal laser does not help the macular oedema** (CVOS).
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **RCOphth (S2), central occlusion: licensed anti-VEGF or the dexamethasone implant are both recommended for the oedema,** chosen with the patient by injection frequency and the risks of pressure rise and cataract. Adding grid laser or PRP to injections gives no benefit.
claims.locator: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists (UK), RVO Guidelines 2022/SCI/359, 'Clinical Guidelines: Retinal Vein Occlusion (RVO)', January 2022 (date of review January 2025; PDF re-posted June 2026), https://www.rcophth.ac.uk/guidance-resources/retinal-vein-occlusion-guideline/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Inject monthly until vision is at its best and stable:** a little over a third reach it after 3 injections and another third need 6. On an as-needed regimen, review every 4–8 weeks. Delaying the start by up to 6 months cost vision, so begin once the diagnosis is made unless a deferral is agreed.
claims.locator: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists (UK), RVO Guidelines 2022/SCI/359, 'Clinical Guidelines: Retinal Vein Occlusion (RVO)', January 2022 (date of review January 2025; PDF re-posted June 2026), https://www.rcophth.ac.uk/guidance-resources/retinal-vein-occlusion-guideline/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **When to stop in poor-vision eyes (S2):** with presenting vision below 6/96, reconsider if neither acuity nor OCT thickness improves after 3 monthly loading injections, and do not go on if there is no response after 6. In ischaemic central occlusion, stop after 3 injections if the oedema clears with no visual gain; but do not exclude eyes with more than 10 disc areas of non-perfusion, or vision of 6/96 or worse with significant oedema, from a trial.
claims.locator: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists (UK), RVO Guidelines 2022/SCI/359, 'Clinical Guidelines: Retinal Vein Occlusion (RVO)', January 2022 (date of review January 2025; PDF re-posted June 2026), https://www.rcophth.ac.uk/guidance-resources/retinal-vein-occlusion-guideline/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Branch occlusion (S2): mild, recent loss can be watched for the first 3 months,** but with marked loss only 18–41% of eyes improve unaided, on average not to 6/12, so treat early. Licensed anti-VEGF or the dexamethasone implant are both recommended. Reserve grid laser for oedema of at least 3 months with vision of 6/12 or worse, no significant macular haemorrhage and a perfused fovea on angiography.
claims.locator: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists (UK), RVO Guidelines 2022/SCI/359, 'Clinical Guidelines: Retinal Vein Occlusion (RVO)', January 2022 (date of review January 2025; PDF re-posted June 2026), https://www.rcophth.ac.uk/guidance-resources/retinal-vein-occlusion-guideline/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Neovascularisation:** in branch occlusion with retinal new vessels, laser the non-perfused area to cut the risk of vitreous haemorrhage. In central occlusion with retinal or iris new vessels, give dense peripheral panretinal laser. An anti-VEGF injection first gives short-term control and can make full laser easier.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ischaemic central occlusion (S2): check monthly for iris or angle new vessels,** and every 1–2 months in the first year after anti-VEGF stops. At the first sign of them give anti-VEGF, then enough PRP on the same day (before the injection) or within 1–2 weeks. With a dexamethasone implant, finding iris vessels early is vital.
claims.locator: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists (UK), RVO Guidelines 2022/SCI/359, 'Clinical Guidelines: Retinal Vein Occlusion (RVO)', January 2022 (date of review January 2025; PDF re-posted June 2026), https://www.rcophth.ac.uk/guidance-resources/retinal-vein-occlusion-guideline/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Established neovascular glaucoma:** if the eye has any visual potential, control the pressure with drops, surgery or cyclo-ablation; regression of the iris and angle vessels helps long-term comfort.
claims.locator: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists (UK), RVO Guidelines 2022/SCI/359, 'Clinical Guidelines: Retinal Vein Occlusion (RVO)', January 2022 (date of review January 2025; PDF re-posted June 2026), https://www.rcophth.ac.uk/guidance-resources/retinal-vein-occlusion-guideline/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Branch occlusion new vessels (S2): sector laser to the ischaemic retina once disc or retinal new vessels appear;** evidence suggests waiting for a vitreous haemorrhage does not harm the outlook, and angiography is not usually needed first. Review every 3–4 months if a quadrant or more is ischaemic. A quadrant usually takes at least 500 burns of 500 µm, 1 burn-width apart, to a mild grey-white.
claims.locator: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists (UK), RVO Guidelines 2022/SCI/359, 'Clinical Guidelines: Retinal Vein Occlusion (RVO)', January 2022 (date of review January 2025; PDF re-posted June 2026), https://www.rcophth.ac.uk/guidance-resources/retinal-vein-occlusion-guideline/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Central occlusion: check the iris and angle (undilated slit lamp and gonioscopy) as often as monthly for 6 months,** and again in ischaemic central occlusion after anti-VEGF stops, to catch new vessels early.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refer every patient to their GP for the systemic conditions, share the results, and tell both about the risk to the other eye.** Offer counselling, vision rehabilitation and social support when vision is lost despite treatment.
claims.locator: American Academy of Ophthalmology PPP Retina/Vitreous Committee (Kovach JL et al.), Ophthalmology, 'Retinal Vein Occlusions Preferred Practice Pattern (2024, updated 2026)', approved 13 September 2024; published Feb 2025; updated June 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2024.12.025), https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/retinal-vein-occlusions-ppp, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Follow-up with significant ischaemia (S2): monthly for 6 months, then 3-monthly to 1 year.** Uncomplicated cases rarely need review beyond 3 years, and disc collaterals with spontaneous resolution of the oedema allow discharge after 6 months.
claims.locator: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists (UK), RVO Guidelines 2022/SCI/359, 'Clinical Guidelines: Retinal Vein Occlusion (RVO)', January 2022 (date of review January 2025; PDF re-posted June 2026), https://www.rcophth.ac.uk/guidance-resources/retinal-vein-occlusion-guideline/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Service standards (UK, S2):** see and treat within 2–4 weeks of presentation, starting treatment within 1–2 weeks of the specialist assessment. Offer low-vision support early, without waiting until every treatment has been tried.
claims.locator: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists (UK), RVO Guidelines 2022/SCI/359, 'Clinical Guidelines: Retinal Vein Occlusion (RVO)', January 2022 (date of review January 2025; PDF re-posted June 2026), https://www.rcophth.ac.uk/guidance-resources/retinal-vein-occlusion-guideline/, retrieved 2026-09-24
